definitions.explanation: Suffix naming a prepared substance that acts on something — a medicine, a cleaning product, an additive, or an industrial chemical. Attached to a noun or verb stem describing what the substance does: {洗|せん}{剤|ざい} washes, {接着|せっちゃく}{剤|ざい} bonds.

examples.japanese: {洗|せん}{剤|ざい}を{切|き}らしてしまった。
{痛|いた}み{止|ど}めの{錠|じょう}{剤|ざい}を{飲|の}んだ。
{接着|せっちゃく}{剤|ざい}が{乾|かわ}くまで{動|うご}かさないでください。
examples.english: Please don't move it until the adhesive dries.

examples.japanese: この{食品|しょくひん}には{保存|ほぞん}{料|りょう}も{着色|ちゃくしょく}{料|りょう}も{使|つか}われていないが、{乾燥|かんそう}{剤|ざい}が{入|はい}っている。
examples.english: This food contains no preservatives or coloring, but there is a desiccant packet inside.

notes:
Highly productive: once you know the suffix, an unfamiliar 〜{剤|ざい} word can usually be decoded from the element in front of it. Note the rendaku — {剤|ざい}, not {さい}.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {洗|せん}{剤|ざい}: detergent
- {錠|じょう}{剤|ざい}: tablet; pill
- {接着|せっちゃく}{剤|ざい}: adhesive; glue
- {殺虫|さっちゅう}{剤|ざい}: insecticide
- {消毒|しょうどく}{剤|ざい}: disinfectant
- {乾燥|かんそう}{剤|ざい}: desiccant
- {鎮痛|ちんつう}{剤|ざい}: painkiller
- カビ{取|と}り{剤|ざい}: mold remover

SIMILAR WORDS:
- 〜{薬|やく}: medicine — for drugs named by what they treat ({胃|い}{薬|ぐすり}, {睡眠|すいみん}{薬|やく}); 〜{剤|ざい} leans toward the prepared form or chemical action
- 〜{料|りょう}: agent added to something — {調味|ちょうみ}{料|りょう} seasoning, {保存|ほぞん}{料|りょう} preservative; used for food additives where 〜{剤|ざい} would sound industrial
